name: Papua New Guinea
headline: Papua New Guinea: +6.2% growth in 2025, 4.4% inflation, debt 52% of GDP
sections: Papua New Guinea is a $33.1 billion economy (2025), the world's 115th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +6.2% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $5,215 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 1.6% of GDP (2024).
Consumer prices rose 4.4% in 2025, above typical targets. Unemployment stood at 2.6% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 3.8% (2025).
Gross government debt is 52% of GDP (2025), a moderate level. The general government balance is −2.1% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +14.3% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Net FDI inflows were −3.6% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 32% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 66.3 years (2024). Population: 10.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
